Earlier reports indicated that Apple had shelved the long-rumored all-glass iPhone (originally intended as a major design to celebrate the iPhone's 20th anniversary), but according to Bloomberg, the redesign is still on track to debut on Pro models next year. Here are the details.

Bloomberg says the redesign is proceeding as planned

Investment analysis firm Jefferies downgraded Apple's stock rating this morning, citing supply chain surveys showing that Apple has abandoned the rumored all-glass iPhone project planned to celebrate the iPhone's 20th anniversary next year.

Bloomberg now reports that the company "expects to launch an iPhone Pro model with a brand-new glass-textured appearance next year," adding that "the front and back of the phone will both use glass (internal codenames V73 and V74), with the glass material extending to both sides of the device, connected by a metal frame in the middle."

However, the report notes that the project has undergone changes since its original conception:

The report further directly contradicts the research note issued by Jefferies this morning, stating that "there have been no changes to Apple's product roadmap."

Jefferies' claims

Jefferies analyst Edison Lee said this morning that, according to the firm's supply chain surveys, the all-glass iPhone has been cancelled due to poor production yields.

Lee described this development as a "significant setback" for Apple's strategy of pushing higher-priced iPhones amid rising memory costs, and noted that cancelling the plan could affect Apple's ability to raise the average selling price and margins of its Pro models.

As a result, Jefferies downgraded Apple's stock rating and cut its target price from US$285.56 to US$263.66. Prior to this, Jefferies had already lowered its target price from US$308.92 on July 31, after Apple reported its Q3 results for fiscal year 2026 and issued cautious guidance for the fourth quarter.
